is_the_span_rule_already_failing_anywher.verdict: No. Under the frozen bold-only parser every filing opens one or two spans of 7 to 31 blocks, which is the size of an audit report, and Pfizer's single unclosed opening excludes nothing by design. So this is a latent failure mode the underline probe made visible, not a live defect - a filer who bolds an index line for that report would trigger it, and none here does.

blast_radius_measured.question: The previous section left this open: widen leading_emphasis in a successor of text_coverage, which every route reading that parser inherits, or recompute emphasis for D01 alone. The parser was patched in one probe process - nothing on disk changed - and D01, D02 and C02 were re-derived for every company. Block splitting does not depend on emphasis, so the block sequence is identical on both sides and the diff is over what each selector chose.

result.D01: Only Marriott moves, by exactly the four headings. The other eight are byte-identical.
result.D02: Two companies move, and the net is clearly negative.

the_five_blocks_it_would_lose.mechanism: Not a black box. audit_report_spans opens an exclusion at any block whose leading_emphasis matches the audit-report title and closes it at the next signature or tenure sentence. Southwest's index line for that report is underlined rather than bold, so admitting underline turns the index line into a title: a third span opens at block 1421 and closes at block 2270 - the real report's signature, 849 blocks later - swallowing everything between.
the_five_blocks_it_would_lose.why_they_matter: These are the same five this repository's keyword-proxy census read against the filing and judged correct: 1428 is the post-storm contingency in the basis-of-presentation note, and 1580/1581/1584/1585 are the military-leave and 2019 customer-agent class actions. So the shared widening would trade five confirmed disclosures for one.

the_one_block_it_would_gain.what_it_is: An underlined-italic case-name caption sitting between two class-action paragraphs in the legal-proceedings note, so admitting underline would correctly add it. It is recorded because the trade is five for one, not five for nothing.

blast_radius_measured.what_this_decides: SUPERSEDED - see the_hazard_was_the_span_rule_not_the_emphasis_rule below. The sentence this field held ('the repair is scoped to D01, not to the shared parser') was true of the widening alone and stopped one measurement too early.

direction_one_what_was_taken.verdict: Every emphasized block the selector refused was refused correctly: Pfizer's twenty are ten pages of a running head (registrant name plus page number) and Salesforce's two are bullet glyphs. No spurious heading was found in any of the nine readable filings.

direction_three_are_the_headings_taken_h.method: The heading list each filing returns, read against the filing. Direction one asks whether the refusals are right and direction two whether anything visually marked was left; neither can see a heading that was taken and is not one.

one_defect_found.not_repaired: One instance in nine filings. 'An unemphasised gap of punctuation only does not end the run' has exactly one example behind it, and a rule written from one example is the kind that fails on the next filing. Registered as D01_PARAMOUNT_2025_HEADING_TRUNCATED_AT_AN_UNBOLDED_PERIOD.
one_defect_found.the_filing_says: Failures to comply with or changes in U.S. or foreign laws or regulations could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition or results of operations.
one_defect_found.why: The filer marks the periods in 'U.S.' with font-weight:400 between bold letters. leading_emphasis is the leading contiguous run of emphasised parts, so it ends at the first unbolded part.
one_defect_found.why_the_common_case_is_not_a_defect: Twenty-six of Ford's thirty and thirty-two of Marriott's thirty-four headings also have a prefix shorter than their block, and in every one the emphasis does not resume: that is the deliberate case the frozen docstring names, a bold lead sentence kept apart from its paragraph. Only Paramount's resumes.

direction_three_are_the_headings_taken_h.what_they_contain: Risk-category headings plus individual risk-factor headings - what the approved definition asks for ('heading-level summary or topic list'). No page furniture, no lead-in sentences, no audit-report text. Ford, Macy's, Enphase, Lumen, Salesforce, Southwest and Paramount all carry their category headings because they bold them; Marriott's are the underlined ones this file is about.

direction_two_what_was_left.corroborated_elsewhere_in_this_repositor: The D02 incorporated-scope work recorded Marriott's heading style as underline plus indentation, measured for another purpose on other sections. Two independent readings landing on the same filer's style is stronger than either alone.

scope_of_the_defect.underline_without_bold_in_item_1a: Marriott only. Across the nine readable filings it is the single filer whose Item 1A carries an underlined, non-bold, non-furniture block, and every one of them is a risk-category heading.
scope_of_the_defect.why_the_fix_is_not_just_add_italic_too: Ford marks fourteen running heads (`Item 1A. Risk Factors (Continued)`) in italic, and Pfizer and Salesforce each open Item 1A with an italic lead-in sentence. Admitting italic would take those seventeen blocks. The measured rule is underline, not emphasis in general.

direction_two_what_was_left.the_defect: text_coverage's leading_emphasis is bold only - <b>, <strong>, <h1>-<h6>, or font-weight >= 600. A filer who marks a heading with underline instead loses it, and nothing in the result says a heading was there.
direction_two_what_was_left.the_in_document_control: Marriott marks its two top-level risk groups with font-weight:700 and its four second-level groups with font-weight:400 plus text-decoration:underline, inside the same <div style="margin-top:9pt;text-indent:22.5pt"> wrapper and the same 10pt Times face. So the same document marks the same structural level two ways, and the result carries one way and not the other - which is why this is not a judgement about what looks like a heading.
direction_two_what_was_left.what_the_approved_definition_asks_for: 02_指标定义 D01: source 10-K Item 1A, output a heading-level summary or topic list. The target is headings. The Spec's own interpretation string says VERBATIM_EMPHASIZED_ITEM_1A_DISCLOSURES, and reading `emphasized` as `bold` rather than `marked by the filer as a heading` is where the two part company.

method: For every block inside the located ITEM_1A scope, the properties the frozen selector keys on (leading_emphasis, linked, the item/part label test, the registrant-name test) plus the enclosing <span>'s style read from the filing's own bytes - not from the parse, because the parse is what is under suspicion.

not_repaired_and_why_not_yet.blast_radius_to_decide_first: Measured - see blast_radius_measured. Widening the shared parser removes five confirmed D02 disclosures on Southwest to gain one on Lumen, so the repair belongs to D01 alone.
not_repaired_and_why_not_yet.where_the_rule_lives: leading_emphasis is computed in scripts/vnext/text_coverage.py, whose bytes issue_28_v11 names and which is checked on both roots. A repair needs a successor rule file in this generation, as D02's section boundary and item capacity did, and that moves the Requirement closure.
not_repaired_and_why_not_yet.why_not_in_this_round: A batch is running on the current closure and is the evidence for it. Changing the closure underneath a report makes the report describe a version that was never run - which this Issue has already recorded once, on a C04 end-to-end run.

the_hazard_was_the_span_rule_not_the_emp.correction: The previous conclusion - repair D01 alone because widening the shared parser costs five confirmed D02 blocks - is withdrawn. The five were not lost to the emphasis rule; they were lost to audit_report_spans opening on a block that a widened parser makes emphasized. Asking what distinguishes that block answers it in one property.

measured_cost.why_a_successor_can_be_small: Section boundaries do not depend on emphasis - _heading reads `linked` and text only - and the measurement confirms the block sequence is identical on both sides. So a successor can run the frozen build_text_document for all of its identity validation and sections, re-run a _Blocks subclass whose only override adds underline, require the block texts and offsets to be identical, and replace the two emphasis fields. That requirement is the guarantee: it makes the successor provably a one-field change rather than a second parser.

what_distinguishes_the_index_line.why_this_is_not_an_invented_criterion: `not linked` is the check _note_heading makes in the same module, three hundred lines above, for the same reason: a hyperlinked copy of a heading is an index entry, not the heading. audit_report_spans keys on leading_emphasis alone and never asked.

the_hazard_was_the_span_rule_not_the_emp.what_is_still_open: Whether underline-without-bold marks something other than a heading in a filing this repository does not hold. Nine filings, one period each, and one filer that uses the style - so the rule rests on an in-document control rather than on a population.

what_this_is: Both directions over D01's Item 1A selection: what the selector took, and what it left. Every D01 check before this one could only ask whether the headings returned are headings; a selector can judge each block it takes correctly and still drop a disclosure, which is the shape the D02 reading found twice.
